input.quote: 12.2 Parties shall obtain Allocated Capacity in the form of MIU on an ownership basis as shown in Schedule C, in return for their financial investment as identified in Schedule B.
input.rationale:
This is a co-ownership consortium C&MA, not a vendor supply contract, and the payment obligations on Teleglobe USA are not a vendor-imposed take-or-pay. Under §12.2 we pay only for the Allocated Capacity (MIUs) we actually own, and §§7.1–7.2 allocate Capital Costs and O&M Costs pro rata to the Investment Share in Schedule B — the same obligation binds every other Party symmetrically, so the commitment is mutual and value-matched rather than a minimum purchase imposed on us. The MIU is a granularity unit ("minimum unit of investment"), not a volume floor, and there are no shortfall penalties: §§7.6 and 7.7 operate as a true-up ("appropriate adjustments will be made in subsequent bills"; final settlement "in order that each Party may bear its proper share of the costs"), with financial charges capped at 120 days (§7.8). Reduction/exit relief exists: no Party can be forced to fund an upgrade or Design Capacity increase (§§13.2, 14.1), interests may be assigned or sold with Management Committee consent that "must not unreasonably withheld or delayed" (§22.2) or freely to affiliates/successors (§§22.3–22.5), IRU capacity may be sold (Schedule D), and participation is terminable on one year's notice after the Initial Period (§18.1). Two points sit short of the preferred position and are noted rather than redlined: the 25-year Initial Period with no unilateral mid-term termination (§18.1), and the rule that "No credit for capital costs will be made to a Party that terminates its participation" (§18.5, p0233). Both are structural to joint ownership of a submarine cable — the funding obligation is the consideration for the ownership interest and capacity we receive — so narrowing them to a 12-month, 30-day-reducible commitment would be disproportionate and would unwind the bargain. No redline proposed; we flag the lock-in and no-capital-credit rule for commercial awareness only.</rationale>
